definitions.explanation: Payment made to an author, composer, or other creator based on the sales of their work, typically calculated as a percentage of sales.

examples.japanese: この{本|ほん}の{印税|いんぜい}は{売|う}り{上|あ}げの10%だ。
examples.english: The royalty for this book is 10% of sales.

examples.japanese: {作家|さっか}は{印税|いんぜい}で{生活|せいかつ}している。
examples.english: The author makes a living from royalties.

examples.japanese: {印税|いんぜい}{収入|しゅうにゅう}だけでは{足|た}りない。

notes:
ETYMOLOGY: {印税|いんぜい} literally means "stamp tax" - {印|いん} refers to the stamp or seal verifying each printed copy, and {税|ぜい} means tax. Historically, authors received payment based on the number of copies stamped.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{印税|いんぜい}が{入|はい}る (to receive royalties)
・{印税|いんぜい}{収入|しゅうにゅう} (royalty income)
・{印税|いんぜい}{契約|けいやく} (royalty agreement)
・{印税|いんぜい}{率|りつ} (royalty rate)

TYPICAL RATES: In Japan, typical book royalty rates range from 5-15% of the cover price, with 10% being common for established authors.

OTHER TYPES OF ROYALTIES:
・{著作権|ちょさくけん}{料|りょう} - copyright fee
・ロイヤリティ/ロイヤルティ - royalty (loanword, used for licensing, franchises)
・{使用料|しようりょう} - usage fee
